title.zh: 卷一百二十 載記第二十 李特 李流
title.en: Volume 120 Records 20: Li Te; Li Liu
title.raw: 卷一百二十 載記第二十 李特 李流 Volume 120 Records 20: Li Te; Li Liu

sentences.zh: 李特，字玄休，巴西宕渠人，其先廩君之苗裔也。

translations.literal: Li Te, courtesy Xuanxiu, was a man of Dangqu in Baxi; his ancestors were descendants of Lord Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te, whose courtesy name was Xuanxiu, came from Dangqu in Baxi commandery and traced his descent from Lord Lin, the legendary ancestor of the Ba peoples.

sentences.zh: 昔武落鐘離山崩，有石穴二所，其一赤如丹，一黑如漆。

translations.literal: Of old Mount Wuluozhongli collapsed; there were two stone caves, one red as cinnabar, one black as lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Mount Wuluozhongli collapsed, leaving two stone caves: one glowed red like cinnabar, the other was black as lacquer.

sentences.zh: 有人出於赤穴者，名曰務相，姓巴氏。

translations.literal: One who came out of the red cave was named Wuxiang, surname Ba.
translations.idiomatic: From the red cave emerged a man named Wuxiang of the Ba clan.

sentences.zh: 有出於黑穴者，凡四姓：曰皥氏、樊氏、柏氏、鄭氏。

translations.literal: Those who came out of the black cave were of four surnames: called the Gao, Fan, Bai, and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Those who emerged from the black cave belonged to four lineages: the Gao, Fan, Bai, and Zheng families.

sentences.zh: 五姓俱出，皆爭為神，於是相與以劍刺穴屋，能著者以為廩君。

translations.literal: The five surnames all came forth and each strove to be god; thereupon together they stabbed with swords at the cave roof—whoever could stick fast would be Lord Lin.
translations.idiomatic: All five clans came forward, each claiming divine right, so they agreed to thrust their swords into the cave roof; whoever could make his blade hold fast would be proclaimed Lord Lin.

sentences.zh: 四姓莫著，而務相之劍懸焉。

translations.literal: The four surnames none stuck; but Wuxiang's sword hung there.
translations.idiomatic: None of the four families managed to lodge a blade, yet Wuxiang's sword caught and hung fast.

sentences.zh: 又以土為船，雕畫之而浮水中，曰：「若其船浮存者，以為廩君。

translations.literal: Again they made boats of earth, carved and painted them, and floated them in the water, saying: If whose boat floats and survives, him they shall take as Lord Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Next they molded boats from clay, carved and painted them, and set them afloat, declaring that whoever kept his boat riding on the water would be Lord Lin.

sentences.zh: 」務相船又獨浮。

translations.literal: Wuxiang's boat again alone floated.
translations.idiomatic: Once again only Wuxiang's boat stayed up.

sentences.zh: 於是遂稱廩君，乘其土船，將其徒卒，當夷水而下，至於鹽陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was titled Lord Lin; riding his earth boat, leading his followers and soldiers, he went down along the Yi River as far as Yanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was acclaimed Lord Lin, sailed his clay boat downstream on the Yi River with his warriors, and reached Yanyang.

sentences.zh: 鹽陽水神女子止廩君曰：「此魚鹽所有，地又廣大，與君俱生，可止無行。

translations.literal: The goddess of the Yanyang waters, a woman, stopped Lord Lin and said: Here fish and salt abound; the land is vast; together with you I could live—stay and do not go.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanyang the river goddess appeared as a woman and barred his way: "Here lie fish and salt in plenty and broad lands besides; stay and build a life with me—do not march on."

sentences.zh: 」廩君曰：「我當為君求廩地，不能止也。

translations.literal: Lord Lin said: I ought for you seek grain land—I cannot stop.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Lin replied: "I must win you fertile fields worthy of a lord; I cannot linger here."

sentences.zh: 」鹽神夜從廩君宿，旦輒去為飛蟲，諸神皆從其飛，蔽日晝昏。

translations.literal: The salt goddess by night followed Lord Lin to lodge; at dawn she always departed, becoming flying insects; the host of gods all followed her flying; they covered the sun and day grew dark.
translations.idiomatic: Each night the salt goddess shared Lord Lin's camp; each dawn she slipped away as swarms of flying insects, and lesser spirits rose with her until their wings eclipsed the sun and turned noon to dusk.

sentences.zh: 廩君欲殺之不可，別又不知天地東西。

translations.literal: Lord Lin wished to kill her but could not; apart, again he did not know heaven-earth east-west.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Lin could not strike her down in that guise, and when she veiled the sky he lost all sense of east and west.

sentences.zh: 如此者十日，廩君乃以青縷遺鹽神曰：「嬰此，即宜之，與汝俱生。

translations.literal: Thus for ten days; Lord Lin then with blue thread gifted the salt goddess, saying: Wear this—then it suits—together with you live.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days of this, Lord Lin sent the goddess a coil of blue silk thread and said: "Wear this about your neck if the match pleases you; then we may live together."

sentences.zh: 弗宜，將去汝。

translations.literal: If not suited, I will leave you.
translations.idiomatic: If it does not suit you, I shall leave you behind."

sentences.zh: 」鹽神受而嬰之。

translations.literal: The salt goddess received and wore it.
translations.idiomatic: She accepted the thread and tied it about her neck.

sentences.zh: 廩君立碭石之上，望膺有青縷者，跪而射之，中鹽神。

translations.literal: Lord Lin stood atop a Yang stone; looking at chests that had blue thread, kneeling he shot them; hit the salt goddess.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Lin took station on a dolmen; wherever he saw the blue thread at a breast he knelt, drew his bow, and shot—and pierced the salt goddess.

sentences.zh: 鹽神死，群神與俱飛者皆去，天乃開朗。

translations.literal: The salt goddess died; the host of gods that together flew with her all departed; heaven then opened bright.
translations.idiomatic: When the salt goddess fell, the spirits that had ridden her drafts scattered, and daylight broke through.

sentences.zh: 廩君復乘土船，下及夷城。

translations.literal: Lord Lin again rode the earth boat, went down and reached Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Lin boarded his clay boat once more and descended to Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 夷城石岸曲，泉水亦曲。

translations.literal: Yicheng's stone bank curved; the spring water also curved.
translations.idiomatic: At Yicheng the riverbank curved like a bow, and the spring wound along with it.

sentences.zh: 廩君望如穴狀，歎曰：「我新從穴中出，今又入此，奈何！

translations.literal: Lord Lin looked—it was like a cave shape; he sighed and said: I newly from within a cave came out; now again I enter this—what to do!
translations.idiomatic: The bend looked to Lord Lin like another cavern mouth, and he sighed: "I have only just left the stone caves—am I to enter a cave again?"

sentences.zh: 」岸即為崩，廣三丈餘，而階陛相乘，廩君登之。

translations.literal: The bank then for him collapsed, wide more than three zhang, and steps and stairways piled one on another; Lord Lin climbed them.
translations.idiomatic: At once the cliff face split open more than three zhang wide, terraced ledges stacking upward like steps, and Lord Lin climbed them to safety.

sentences.zh: 岸上有平石方一丈，長五尺，廩君休其上，投策計算，皆著石焉，因立城其旁而居之。

translations.literal: On the bank was a flat stone one zhang square, five chi long; Lord Lin rested on it, cast counting-rods to reckon—all landed on the stone; therefore he founded a city beside it and dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: On the heights lay a flat slab ten feet square and five feet long; Lord Lin rested there, cast his divining stalks, and every stalk settled true upon the rock, so he walled a city beside it and made his seat.

sentences.zh: 其後種類遂繁。

translations.literal: Afterward their kinds then multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: From that stock the Ba peoples multiplied.

sentences.zh: 秦並天下，以為黔中郡，薄賦斂之，口歲出錢四十。

translations.literal: Qin united the realm and made it Qianzhong commandery; lightly they taxed it; per mouth yearly issued forty cash.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin unified the empire it folded the region into Qianzhong commandery and levied light taxes—forty cash per person each year.

sentences.zh: 巴人呼賦為賨，因謂之賨人焉。

translations.literal: The Ba people called tax 'cong'; therefore they were called cong people.
translations.idiomatic: The Ba called their poll tax cong, and so people spoke of them as the Cong people.

sentences.zh: 及漢高祖為漢王，募賨人平定三秦。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu was king of Han, he recruited cong people to pacify the Three Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bang held the title King of Han, he enlisted Cong warriors to bring the Three Qin to heel.

sentences.zh: 既而求還鄉里，高祖以其功，復同豐、沛，不供賦稅，更名其地為巴郡。

translations.literal: Afterward they sought return to villages; Gaozu for their merit treated them again like Feng and Pei—not supplying tax-and-rent; he renamed their territory Ba commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When they wished to go home, Gaozu rewarded their service with the same exemption enjoyed by his old Feng and Pei followers—no grain or cloth levy—and redesignated their lands as Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 土有鹽鐵丹漆之饒，俗性剽勇，又善歌舞。

translations.literal: The soil had abundance of salt, iron, cinnabar, lacquer; custom nature fierce brave; also skilled in song and dance.
translations.idiomatic: The region was rich in salt, iron, vermilion, and lacquer; the people were fierce by temperament and gifted in song and dance.

sentences.zh: 高祖愛其舞，詔樂府習之，今《巴渝舞》是也。

translations.literal: Gaozu loved their dance; he ordered the Music Bureau to practice it—today's 'Bayu Dance' is this.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu delighted in their dances and ordered the imperial music office to preserve them—the performance survives as the Bayu suite.

sentences.zh: 漢末，張魯居漢中，以鬼道教百姓，賨人敬信巫覡，多往奉之。

translations.literal: At Han's end, Zhang Lu dwelt in Hanzhong; with ghost-Dao he taught the hundred surnames; cong people revered and trusted shamans; many went to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Han, Zhang Lu ruled Hanzhong and instructed the people with his spirit cult; the Cong honoured shamans and many flocked to Zhang's altars.

sentences.zh: 值天下大亂，自巴西之宕渠遷于漢中楊車阪，抄掠行旅，百姓患之，號為楊車巴。

translations.literal: They encountered realm great chaos; from Baxi's Dangqu they moved to Hanzhong's Yangche Slope; they plundered travelers; hundred surnames suffered them; they were titled Yangche Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the turmoil they quit Dangqu in Baxi for Yangche Slope in Hanzhong, waylaid merchants, and terrorized the countryside until folk nicknamed them the Yangche Ba.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝克漢中，特祖將五百餘家歸之，魏武帝拜為將軍，遷于略陽，北土復號之為巴氐。

translations.literal: Wei Wudi conquered Hanzhong; Li Te's grandfather led more than five hundred households to submit; Wei Wudi appointed him general and transferred him to Lüeyang; northern lands again called them Ba Di.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao took Hanzhong, Li Te's grandfather brought five hundred-odd households over to serve him; Cao enfeoffed him as a general and resettled the clan in Lüeyang, where northerners again labelled them Ba Di.

sentences.zh: 特父慕，為東羌獵將。

translations.literal: Li Te's father Mu was Eastern Qiang hunt general.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te's father Li Mu served as hunt general among the eastern Qiang auxiliaries.

sentences.zh: 特少仕州郡，見異當時，身長八尺，雄武善騎射，沈毅有大度。

translations.literal: Te in youth served province and commandery; was viewed strange in that age; body eight chi tall; heroic martial skilled riding-shooting; deep firm had great capacity.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Li Te served in provincial posts and stood out from his peers: he stood eight chi tall, bold in arms, expert with horse and bow, steady of temper and broad-minded.

sentences.zh: 元康中，氐齊萬年反，關西擾亂，頻歲大饑，百姓乃流移就穀，相與入漢川者數萬家。

translations.literal: In Yuankang, the Di Qi Wannian rebelled; Guanxi was disturbed; successive years great famine; hundred surnames then drifted moved seeking grain; together entering Han River lands were several ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuankang the Di leader Qi Wannian rose in revolt and threw the northwest into turmoil; famine struck year after year, so commoners migrated toward grain—tens of thousands of households poured into the Han River basin together.

sentences.zh: 特隨流人將入於蜀，至劍閣，箕踞太息，顧眄險阻曰：「劉禪有如此之地而面縛於人，豈非庸才邪！

translations.literal: Te followed drifting people about to enter Shu; arriving at Jiange, he squatted sprawling and sighed greatly; looking askance at the peril defiles said: Liu Shan had such lands yet face-bound before others—is it not mediocrity!
translations.idiomatic: Li Te marched with the refugees toward Shu. At Jiange Pass he sprawled on his seat, drew a long breath, and swept his eyes along the sheer defiles: "Liu Shan held terrain like this yet went bound captive to his foes—could anything speak more of mediocrity?"

sentences.zh: 」同移者閻式、趙肅、李遠、任回等咸歎異之。

translations.literal: Those who moved together Yan Shi, Zhao Su, Li Yuan, Ren Hui and others all sighed in wonder at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi, Zhao Su, Li Yuan, Ren Hui, and the others who travelled with him murmured in admiration.

sentences.zh: 初，流人既至漢中，上書求寄食巴、蜀，朝議不許，遣侍御史李苾持節慰勞，且監察之，不令入劍閣。

translations.literal: At first, drifting people having reached Hanzhong, memorialized seeking lodged food in Ba and Shu; court deliberation did not permit; sent attendant censor Li Bi holding insignia to console and labour, and moreover supervise them, not ordering entry into Jiange.
translations.idiomatic: When the refugees first reached Hanzhong they petitioned for permission to winter in Ba and Shu; the court refused and dispatched Censor Li Bi with imperial credentials to console them while keeping watch—and barred them from crossing Jiange Pass.

sentences.zh: 苾至漢中，受流人貨賂，反為表曰：「流人十萬餘口，非漢中一郡所能振贍，東下荊州，水湍迅險，又無舟船。

translations.literal: Bi reached Hanzhong, received drifting people's goods-bribes, contrary made memorial saying: Drifting people hundred thousand and more mouths—not Hanzhong one commandery can relieve; east down Jingzhou—waters rapid swift perilous; again no boats.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi entered Hanzhong, pocketed bribes from the refugees, and forwarded a memorial arguing that more than a hundred thousand displaced persons could not be fed from Hanzhong alone; sending them east through Jingzhou meant rushing rapids without boats.

sentences.zh: 蜀有倉儲，人復豐稔，宜令就食。

translations.literal: Shu has granary stores; people again abundant harvest—fit order go eat.
translations.idiomatic: Shu still held government granaries and had enjoyed bumper crops; the court should let them go there for sustenance."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從之，由是散在益、梁，不可禁止。

translations.literal: The court followed it; by this scattered in Yi and Liang—not possible forbid.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted the plea, and the refugees spilled across Yi and Liang until no edict could contain them.

sentences.zh: 廞自稱大都督、大將軍、益州牧。

translations.literal: Xin himself titled grand chief commander, grand general, Yi provincial shepherd.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xin declared himself grand commander-in-chief, grand general, and governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 特弟庠與兄弟及妹夫李含、任回、上官惇、扶風李攀、始平費佗、氐苻成、隗伯等以四千騎歸廞。

translations.literal: Te's younger brother Xiang with brothers and sister's husband Li Han, Ren Hui, Shangguan Dun, Fufeng Li Pan, Shiping Fei Tuo, Di Fu Cheng, Wei Bo and others with four thousand horse submitted to Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te's brother Li Xiang led his kinsmen, brothers-in-law Li Han and Ren Hui, Shangguan Dun, Li Pan of Fufeng, Fei Tuo of Shiping, the Di leaders Fu Cheng and Wei Bo, and four thousand horsemen to Zhao Xin's banner.

sentences.zh: 廞以庠為威寇將軍，使斷北道。

translations.literal: Xin made Xiang awe-bandit general, ordered sever north road.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xin appointed Li Xiang general who awes raiders and tasked him with sealing the northern approaches.

sentences.zh: 庠素東羌良將，曉軍法，不用麾幟，舉矛為行伍，斬部下不用命者三人，部陣肅然。

translations.literal: Xiang was by nature Eastern Qiang fine general; understood army law; did not use banners; raised spear as ranks; beheaded subordinates not obeying orders three men; formation solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang was a seasoned Eastern Qiang commander who knew regulations by heart; he needed no signal drums—lifting his spear aligned the ranks—and executed three unruly soldiers until his formation stood rigid as iron.

sentences.zh: 廞惡其齊整，欲殺之而未言。

translations.literal: Xin hated his neat orderliness; wished kill him yet did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xin resented such disciplined popularity and plotted murder without breathing a word.

sentences.zh: 長史杜淑、司馬張粲言於廞曰：「傳云五大不在邊，將軍起兵始爾，便遣李庠握強兵於外，愚竊惑焉。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Du Shu, aide Zhang Can spoke to Xin saying: Tradition says five greats not at border; general raising troops just now—then send Li Xiang grasp strong troops outside—stupid I privately perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Du Shu and major Zhang Can warned Zhao Xin: "The chronicles say powerful ministers must not hold frontier commands; you have only just raised arms yet Li Xiang already grips a host beyond your walls—this alarms us."

sentences.zh: 且非我族類，其心必異，倒戈授人，竊以為不可，願將軍圖之。

translations.literal: Moreover not our clan kind—their hearts surely different; invert spear give others—I privately deem not acceptable; wish general plan it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover they are not of our kin; their loyalties will differ. Handing them reversed blades invites disaster—we urge you to reconsider."

sentences.zh: 」廞斂容曰：「卿言正當吾意，可謂起予者商，此天使卿等成吾事也。

translations.literal: Xin drew-in manner said: Your words just hit my intent—may be called one who rouses me is Shang—this heaven orders you etc. complete my affair.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xin composed himself and answered: "You speak my mind exactly—you are the merchants who woke Confucius to wisdom; heaven sends you to finish what I began."

sentences.zh: 」會庠在門，請見廞，廞大悅，引庠見之。

translations.literal: Just then Xiang was at gate; requested see Xin; Xin greatly pleased; led Xiang see them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang chose that moment to ask audience at the gate; Zhao Xin welcomed him eagerly and ushered him in before Du Shu and Zhang Can.

sentences.zh: 庠欲觀廞意旨，再拜進曰：「今中國大亂，無復綱維，晉室當不可復興也。

translations.literal: Xiang wished observe Xin's intention; twice bowed advanced saying: Now central plain great chaos; no again guideline cord; Jin house surely not able revive.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang wished to sound Zhao Xin out: bowing twice he urged: "The heartland lies in chaos without ritual or law; the house of Jin cannot rise again."

sentences.zh: 明公道格天地，德被區宇，湯、武之事，實在於今。

translations.literal: Illustrious Duke path matches heaven-earth; virtue covers regional universe—Tang-Wu affairs truly lie in today.
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue spans heaven and earth; the deeds of Cheng Tang and King Wu are ripe today."

sentences.zh: 宜應天時，順人心，拯百姓于塗炭，使物情知所歸，則天下可定，非但庸、蜀而已。

translations.literal: Fit respond heaven season; follow people's hearts; rescue hundred surnames from mud-charcoal; make things' feelings know where return—then realm can settle—not only Yong-Shu alone.
translations.idiomatic: Seize the mandate of the hour, follow men's hearts, lift the people from ruin, and show all creation where loyalty lies—the empire will settle, far beyond Ba and Shu alone."

sentences.zh: ，」廞怒曰：「此豈人臣所宜言！

translations.literal: , Xin angrily said: This how subject fitting speak!
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xin flushed with staged wrath: "What minister may utter such words?"

sentences.zh: 」令淑等議之。

translations.literal: Ordered Shu etc. deliberate it.
translations.idiomatic: He told Du Shu and the others to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 於是淑等上庠大逆不道，廞乃殺之，及其子侄宗族三十餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shu etc. charged Xiang great rebellious not Way; Xin then killed him, together with sons nephews clan kin thirty-odd persons.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shu and his allies memorialized Li Xiang for high treason; Zhao Xin executed him along with more than thirty sons, nephews, and kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 廞慮特等為難，遣人喻之曰：「庠非所宜言，罪應至死，不及兄弟。

translations.literal: Xin worried Te etc. make difficulty; sent person instruct them saying: Xiang not fitting speech—crime ought reach death—not reaching brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Li Te's reaction, Zhao Xin sent messengers: "Li Xiang spoke treason and earned death; his brothers stand innocent."

sentences.zh: 」以庠屍還特，復以特兄弟為督將，以安其眾。

translations.literal: With Xiang corpse return Te; again made Te brothers supervise generals; to pacify their masses.
translations.idiomatic: He returned Li Xiang's body and reappointed Li Te and his brothers as commanders to calm their followers.

sentences.zh: 牙門將許弇求為巴東監軍，杜淑、張粲固執不許。

translations.literal: Gate general Xu Yan sought become Ba East inspector army; Du Shu, Zhang Can stubbornly held not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Gate captain Xu Yan sought the Eastern Ba inspectorate; Du Shu and Zhang Can refused outright.

sentences.zh: 弇怒，于廞閣下手刃殺淑、粲，淑、粲左右又殺弇，皆廞腹心也。

translations.literal: Yan enraged; in Xin's pavilion lower hand blade killed Shu, Can; Shu, Can attendants again killed Yan—all Xin's belly-hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yan burst into Zhao Xin's chamber and cut down Du Shu and Zhang Can; their guards then slew Xu—all were men Zhao Xin trusted.

sentences.zh: 特兄弟既以怨廞，引兵歸綿竹。

translations.literal: Te brothers already thereby resent Xin; led troops return Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: The Li brothers, nursing grievances against Zhao Xin, withdrew their army to Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 廞恐朝廷討己，遣長史費遠、犍為太守李苾、督護常俊督萬餘人斷北道，次綿竹之石亭。

translations.literal: Xin feared court punish self; sent chief clerk Fei Yuan, Qianwei prefect Li Bi, protector Chang Jun supervise ten thousand-odd men sever north road; halted at Mianzhu's Stone Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xin feared imperial punishment and dispatched chief clerk Fei Yuan, Qianwei prefect Li Bi, and protector Chang Jun with ten thousand men to hold the northern road, camping at Stone Pavilion near Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 特密收合得七千餘人，夜襲遠軍，遠大潰，因放火燒之，死者十八九。

translations.literal: Te secretly gathered obtained seven thousand-odd men; night attacked Yuan army; Yuan greatly routed; then set fire burn them—dead eight or nine tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te secretly rallied seven thousand fighters, struck Fei Yuan by night, shattered his host, and set the camps ablaze so that nine in ten died.

sentences.zh: 進攻成都。

translations.literal: Advanced attacked Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 廞聞兵至，驚懼不知所為。

translations.literal: Xin heard troops arrived; alarmed feared knew not what do.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Xin learned troops had arrived he panicked, helpless.

sentences.zh: 李苾、張征等夜斬關走出，文武盡散。

translations.literal: Li Bi, Zhang Zheng etc. night cut gate flee out; civil-military all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi and Zhang Zheng fled through the gates by night; civil and military officers melted away.

sentences.zh: 廞獨與妻子乘小船走至廣都，為下人硃竺所殺。

translations.literal: Xin alone with wife children rode small boat fled reached Guangdu; by servant Zhu Zhu killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xin alone took wife and children by skiff toward Guangdu, where his servant Zhu Zhu murdered him.

sentences.zh: 特至成都，縱兵大掠，害西夷護軍薑發，殺廞長史袁治及廞所置守長，遣其牙門王角、李基詣洛陽陳廞之罪狀。

translations.literal: Te reached Chengdu; unleashed troops great plunder; harmed Western Yi protector Jiang Fa; killed Xin chief clerk Yuan Zhi and Xin-installed guard chiefs; sent his gate Wang Jiao, Li Ji go Luoyang display Xin's crime condition.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te entered Chengdu and let his army sack the city; he executed Protector of the Western Yi Jiang Fa, Zhao Xin's chief clerk Yuan Zhi, and Xin's appointed magistrates, then sent aides Wang Jiao and Li Ji to Luoyang with the indictment of Zhao Xin's crimes.

sentences.zh: 先是，惠帝以梁州刺史羅尚為平西將軍、領護西夷校尉、益州刺史，督牙門將王敦、上庸都尉義歆、蜀郡太守徐儉、廣漢太守辛冉等凡七千餘人入蜀。

translations.literal: Before this, Huidi took Liang provincial inspector Luo Shang as Pacify-West general, concurrently Protect Western Yi colonel, Yi provincial inspector; supervised gate general Wang Dun, Shangfang commandant Yi Xin, Shu commandery prefect Xu Jian, Guanghan prefect Xin Ran etc. altogether seven thousand-odd men enter Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Hui had appointed Liang inspector Luo Shang Pacifier of the West, colonel of the Western Yi, and governor of Yi Province, directing gate captain Wang Dun, Shangyong commandant Yi Xin, Shu prefect Xu Jian, Guanghan prefect Xin Ran, and more than seven thousand troops into Shu.

sentences.zh: 特等聞尚來，甚懼，使其弟驤于道奉迎，並貢寶物。

translations.literal: Te etc. heard Shang come; greatly feared; sent younger brother Xiang on road offer welcome; together tribute treasures.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Te learned Luo Shang was coming he sent his brother Li Xiang ahead with rich gifts to greet him.

sentences.zh: 尚甚悅，以驤為騎督。

translations.literal: Shang greatly pleased; made Xiang horse supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang was delighted and appointed Li Xiang cavalry commandant.

sentences.zh: 特及弟流復以牛酒勞尚於綿竹。

translations.literal: Te and younger brother Liu again with oxen wine labour Shang at Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te and Li Liu later welcomed Luo Shang at Mianzhu with cattle and wine.

sentences.zh: 王敦、辛冉並說尚曰：「特等流人，專為盜賊，急宜梟除，可因會斬之。

translations.literal: Wang Dun, Xin Ran together urged Shang saying: Te etc. drifting people; specialize as bandits—urgent fit decapitate remove—can use banquet behead them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun and Xin Ran both urged Luo Shang: "The Li brothers are rootless refugees turned bandits—strike now; summon them to a banquet and strike off their heads."

sentences.zh: 」尚不納。

translations.literal: Shang did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang refused.

sentences.zh: 冉先與特有舊，因謂特曰：「故人相逢，不吉當凶矣。

translations.literal: Ran formerly with Te had old ties; therefore said to Te: Old friends meet—not auspicious ought ominous.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Ran, who had known Li Te of old, warned him: "When old friends meet in such times, expect ill luck if not outright doom."

sentences.zh: 」特深自猜懼。

translations.literal: Te deeply self suspected feared.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te grew deeply suspicious and afraid.

sentences.zh: 尋有符下秦、雍州，凡流人入漢川者，皆下所在召還。

translations.literal: Soon there was tally issued down Qin, Yong provinces; all drifting people who entered Han River lands—all down localities summon return.
translations.idiomatic: Soon edicts reached Qin and Yong ordering every refugee who had entered the Han basin to report home to their native districts.

sentences.zh: 特兄輔素留鄉里，托言迎家，既至蜀，謂特曰：「中國方亂，不足復還，」特以為然，乃有雄據巴、蜀之意。

translations.literal: Te's elder brother Fu by nature stayed villages; pretended words greet family; having reached Shu, said to Te: Central plain just chaotic—not worth again return; Te deemed it so—then had dominate Ba-Shu intention.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te's elder brother Li Fu had remained behind; claiming he would fetch the family, he reached Shu and told Li Te: "The north is still convulsed—there is nothing to go back to." Li Te agreed and began to dream of holding Ba and Shu.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以討趙廞功，拜特宣威將軍，封長樂鄉侯，流為奮威將軍、武陽侯。

translations.literal: Court for punishing Zhao Xin merit; appointed Te Proclaim Might general; enfeoffed Changle village marquis; Liu was Stir Might general, Wuyang marquis.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in defeating Zhao Xin the court named Li Te general who proclaims might and lord of Changle village, while Li Liu became general who rouses might and marquis of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 璽書下益州，條列六郡流人與特協同討廞者，將加封賞。

translations.literal: Sealed document down Yi Province; item-list six commanderies drifting people with Te cooperated attack Xin—will add enfeoff rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial rescripts reached Yi Province listing refugees from the six commanderies who had aided Li Te against Zhao Xin for enfeoffment and reward.

sentences.zh: 會辛冉以非次見征，不顧應召，又欲以滅廞為己功，乃寢朝命，不以實上。

translations.literal: Just then Xin Ran by irregular saw summons; did not heed respond summon; again wished take destroy Xin as self merit—then slept court order; did not by truth report up.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Ran had been promoted out of turn yet ignored recall orders and hoped to credit himself alone with Zhao Xin's destruction, so he suppressed the court's dispatch and reported falsely.

sentences.zh: 眾咸怨之。

translations.literal: Multitudes all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone resented him for it.

sentences.zh: 羅尚遣從事催遣流人，限七月上道，辛冉性貪暴，欲殺流人首領，取其資貨，乃移檄發遣。

translations.literal: Luo Shang sent clerk urge dispatch drifting people; limit seventh month take road; Xin Ran nature greedy violent; wished kill drifting people chiefs; take their goods wealth—then moved proclamation issue dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang ordered aides to hurry the refugees onto the road by the seventh month. Xin Ran, greedy and cruel, hoped to murder refugee leaders and seize their wealth, so he circulated warrants ordering departure.

sentences.zh: 又令梓潼太守張演于諸要施關，搜索寶貨。

translations.literal: Again ordered Zitong prefect Zhang Yan at various passes set barriers; search treasure goods.
translations.idiomatic: He told Zitong prefect Zhang Yan to throw up barriers on every trunk road and strip refugees of valuables.

sentences.zh: 特等固請，求至秋收。

translations.literal: Te etc. firmly requested; begged reach autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te petitioned repeatedly for delay until the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 流人布在梁、益，為人傭力，及聞州郡逼遣，人人愁怨，不知所為。

translations.literal: Drifting people spread in Liang, Yi; for others hired labour; when heard provinces commanderies force dispatch—each person grief resentment; knew not what do.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees were scattered across Liang and Yi working as hired labor; when word spread that governors were driving them out, every household brooded in fear with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 又知特兄弟頻請求停，皆感而恃之。

translations.literal: Again knew Te brothers repeatedly requested stop—all moved and relied on them.
translations.idiomatic: They knew too that the Li brothers kept pleading for reprieve, so they looked to them with gratitude and trust.

sentences.zh: 且水雨將降，年穀未登，流人無以為行資，遂相與詣特。

translations.literal: Moreover water rain about fall; year grain not ascended; drifting people nothing use as travel capital—thereupon together went to Te.
translations.idiomatic: The rains were due and the year's grain was not yet in; refugees lacked travel money, so they thronged to Li Te together.

sentences.zh: 特乃結大營於綿竹，以處流人，移冉求自寬。

translations.literal: Te then tied great camp at Mianzhu; to house drifting people; moved document to Ran seeking self lenience.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te pitched a great camp at Mianzhu to shelter the refugees and petitioned Xin Ran for mercy.

sentences.zh: 冉大怒，遣人分榜通逵，購募特兄弟，許以重賞。

translations.literal: Ran greatly angry; sent men divide notices on thoroughfares; offer recruit Te brothers; promised heavy rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Ran flew into a rage, plastered the highways with notices, and offered huge bounties for the Li brothers' heads.

sentences.zh: 特見，大懼，悉取以歸，與驤改其購云：「能送六郡之豪李、任、閻、趙、楊、上官及氐、叟侯王一首，賞百匹。

translations.literal: Te saw; greatly feared; all took to return; with Xiang altered its offer saying: Able deliver six commanderies' magnates Li, Ren, Yan, Zhao, Yang, Shangguan and Di, Sou lord-kings one head—reward hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te panicked when he saw them, seized every placard, and with Li Xiang rewrote the reward to read: "One hundred bolts of silk for whoever delivers the head of any magnate among Li, Ren, Yan, Zhao, Yang, Shangguan, or any Di or Sou chieftain from the six commanderies."

sentences.zh: 」流人既不樂移，咸往歸特，騁馬屬鞬，同聲雲集，旬月間眾過二萬。

translations.literal: Drifting people since not happy move—all went submit Te; galloping horses trailing quivers; same voice cloud gathered—ten-day month inside multitude exceeded twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to march away, the refugees rallied to Li Te with saddled horses and shouldered bows until within weeks his host passed twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 流亦聚眾數千。

translations.literal: Liu also gathered multitude several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu likewise assembled several thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 物乃分為二營，特居北營，流居東營。

translations.literal: Things then divided into two camps; Te dwelt north camp; Liu dwelt east camp.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te then split his host into two camps, keeping the northern enclosure himself while Li Liu held the eastern camp.

sentences.zh: 特遣閻式詣羅尚，求申期。

translations.literal: Te sent Yan Shi go Luo Shang; beg extend deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te sent Yan Shi to Luo Shang to beg an extension.

sentences.zh: 式既至，見冉營柵沖要，謀掩流人，歎曰：「無寇而城，仇必保焉。

translations.literal: Shi having arrived; saw Ran camp palisades choke points; plotted surprise drifting people; sighed saying: Without bandits yet wall—enemy surely guards there.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Shi arrived he saw Xin Ran palisading vital crossings to ambush refugees and sighed: "Building fortifications without invaders means someone plans a massacre."

sentences.zh: 今而速之，亂將作矣！

translations.literal: Now yet hurry them—chaos about arise!
translations.idiomatic: Press them now and rebellion follows."

sentences.zh: 」又知冉及李苾意不可回，乃辭尚還綿竹。

translations.literal: Again knew Ran and Li Bi intent not able turn—then took leave Shang returned Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Xin Ran and Li Bi would not bend, he bid Luo Shang farewell and rode back to Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 尚謂式曰：「子且以吾意告諸流人，今聽寬矣。

translations.literal: Shang told Shi: You for now take my intent tell all drifting people—now listen lenient.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang told Yan Shi: "Tell the refugees on my behalf that I grant them temporary relief."

sentences.zh: 」式曰：「明公惑於奸說，恐無寬理。

translations.literal: Shi said: Illustrious sir is deluded by treacherous talk—I fear there is no basis for lenience.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi replied: "My lord has let deceivers sway him; I doubt there will be any real mercy."

sentences.zh: 弱而不可輕者百姓也，今促之不以理，眾怒難犯，恐為禍不淺。

translations.literal: Weak yet not to be slighted—such are the hundred surnames; now urging them without principle—the multitude's wrath is hard to offend—I fear the disaster not shallow.
translations.idiomatic: The common people seem powerless yet must not be slighted; drive them unjustly and popular rage becomes unstoppable—the harm could run very deep."

sentences.zh: 」尚曰：「然。

translations.literal: Shang said: So.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang said: "You have the right of it."

sentences.zh: 吾不欺子，子其行矣。

translations.literal: I do not deceive you—you may go.
translations.idiomatic: I am not misleading you—go on your way."

sentences.zh: 」式至綿竹，言於特曰：「尚雖云爾，然未可必信也。

translations.literal: Shi reached Mianzhu; spoke to Te saying: Shang although spoke thus—yet not possible surely trust.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Shi returned to Mianzhu he warned Li Te: "Luo Shang may promise relief, but his word is not yet proof."

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 尚威刑不立，冉等各擁強兵，一旦為變，亦非尚所能制，深宜為備。

translations.literal: Shang awe-punishment not established; Ran etc. each grasp strong troops—once event mutiny—again not what Shang can control—deeply fit make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang has established no credible authority, while Xin Ran and his fellows command veteran troops; if they stir trouble he cannot rein them in—you must prepare in depth."

sentences.zh: 」特納之。

translations.literal: Te accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te took the warning to heart.

sentences.zh: 冉、苾相與謀曰：「羅侯貪而無斷，日復一日，流人得展奸計。

translations.literal: Ran, Bi together plotted saying: Lord Luo greedy yet without decisiveness—day repeats day—drifting people able unfold treacherous plans.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Ran and Li Bi schemed together: "Luo Shang is grasping and indecisive; day after day the refugees gain room for treachery.

sentences.zh: 李特兄弟並有雄才，吾屬將為豎子虜矣。

translations.literal: Li Te brothers together have heroic talent—we kinds about to become striplings' captives.
translations.idiomatic: The Li brothers are formidable; we are about to be toyed with like boys."

sentences.zh: 宜為決計，不足復問之。

translations.literal: Fit make decisive plan—not worth again ask him.
translations.idiomatic: We must settle this ourselves—there is no point consulting Luo Shang again."

sentences.zh: 乃遣廣漢都尉曾元、牙門張顯、劉並等潛率步騎三萬襲特營。

translations.literal: Then sent Guanghan commandant Zeng Yuan, gate Zhang Xian, Liu Bing etc. secretly lead infantry-cavalry thirty thousand raid Te's camp.
translations.idiomatic: They secretly ordered Guanghan commandant Zeng Yuan, gate captains Zhang Xian and Liu Bing to march thirty thousand foot and horse against Li Te's camp.

sentences.zh: 羅尚聞之，亦遣督護田佐助元。

translations.literal: Luo Shang heard it; also sent protector Tian Zuo assist Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Shang heard the plan he sent protector Tian Zuo to reinforce Zeng Yuan.

sentences.zh: 特素知之，乃繕甲厲兵，戒嚴以待之。

translations.literal: Te by nature knew it; then repaired armor sharpened weapons; alert strict to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te had long expected the strike; he armored his men, honed weapons, and stood ready.

sentences.zh: 元等至，特安臥不動，待其眾半入，發伏擊之，殺傷者甚眾，害田佐、曾元、張顯，傳首以示尚、冉。

translations.literal: Yuan etc. arrived; Te peacefully lay unmoved; waited their multitude half entered; released ambush struck them—wounded killed very many—harmed Tian Zuo, Zeng Yuan, Zhang Xian—sent heads to display to Shang, Ran.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Yuan arrived Li Te feigned calm until half the enemy column had entered his trap, then sprung ambushes that slaughtered legions. Tian Zuo, Zeng Yuan, and Zhang Xian fell; Li Te sent their heads to Luo Shang and Xin Ran.

sentences.zh: 尚謂將佐曰：「此虜成去矣，而廣漢不用吾言，以張賊勢，今將若之何！」

translations.literal: Shang told generals aides saying: These captives succeed gone—yet Guanghan did not use my words—thereby swell bandit power—now about to do what!
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang told his officers: "Those rebels were ripe for removal, yet Guanghan ignored my counsel and swelled the enemy's strength—what are we to do now?"

sentences.zh: 於是六郡流人推特為主。

translations.literal: Thereupon six commanderies drifting people lifted Te as lord.
translations.idiomatic: The refugees from the six commanderies then acclaimed Li Te as their leader.

sentences.zh: 特命六郡人部曲督李含、上邽令任臧、始昌令閻式、諫議大夫李攀、陳倉令李武、陰平令李遠、將兵都尉楊褒等上書，請依梁統奉竇融故事，推特行鎮北大將軍，承制封拜，其弟流行鎮東將軍，以相鎮統。

translations.literal: Te ordered six commanderies men troop supervisors Li Han, Shanggui magistrate Ren Zang, Shichang magistrate Yan Shi, grandee consultant Li Pan, Chencang magistrate Li Wu, Yinping magistrate Li Yuan, commandant of troops Yang Bao etc. memorialize; beg according to Liang Tong submitting Dou Rong precedent—lift Te acting Pacify-North grand general, inherit regulations enfeoff appoint—his younger brother Liu act Pacify-East general—to mutually anchor command.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te had troop supervisor Li Han of the six commanderies, Shanggui prefect Ren Zang, Shichang prefect Yan Shi, counsellor Li Pan, Chencang prefect Li Wu, Yinping prefect Li Yuan, and commandant Yang Bao memorialize the throne, citing how Liang Tong once presented Dou Rong: appoint Li Te acting grand general who pacifies the north with authority to enfeoff officers, and appoint his brother Li Liu grand general who pacifies the east so both wings secure the realm.

sentences.zh: 於是進兵攻冉於廣漢。

translations.literal: Thereupon advanced troops attacked Ran at Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: They marched on Xin Ran in Guanghan commandery.

sentences.zh: 冉眾出戰，特每破之。

translations.literal: Ran multitude went out battle; Te each time routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xin Ran gave battle Li Te broke his lines.

sentences.zh: 尚遣李苾及費遠率眾救冉，憚特不敢進。

translations.literal: Shang sent Li Bi and Fei Yuan lead multitude rescue Ran—feared Te dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang ordered Li Bi and Fei Yuan to relieve Xin Ran, but they feared Li Te and halted.

sentences.zh: 冉智力既窘，出奔江陽。

translations.literal: Ran stratagem strength already exhausted—fled out to Jiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Outmaneuvered, Xin Ran fled to Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 特入據廣漢，以李超為太守，進兵攻尚于成都。

translations.literal: Te entered occupied Guanghan; took Li Chao as grand administrator; advanced troops attacked Shang at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te seized Guanghan, installed Li Chao as prefect, and pushed on Chengdu against Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 閻式遺尚書，責其信用讒構，欲討流人，又陳特兄弟立功王室，以寧益土。

translations.literal: Yan Shi sent letter to court—blamed its trust employ slander framing—wished punish drifting people—again stated Te brothers established merit royal house—to pacify Yi soil.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi addressed the secretariat, condemning the court for crediting slander against the refugees even as the Li brothers had served the dynasty and restored peace to Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 尚覽書，知特等將有大志，嬰城固守，求救于梁、寧二州。

translations.literal: Shang read letter—knew Te etc. about have great ambition—ring city firmly guard—beg rescue from Liang, Ning two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the memorial Luo Shang realized Li Te harboured loftier ambitions; he drew up his walls and appealed for relief from Liang and Ning provinces.

sentences.zh: 於是特自稱使持節、大都督、鎮北大將軍，承制封拜一依竇融在河西故事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Te self titled commissioner-with-credentials, grand chief commander, Pacify-North grand general—inheriting regulations enfeoff appointments wholly followed Dou Rong at Hexi precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te then proclaimed himself commissioner bearing credentials, commander-in-chief, and grand general who pacifies the north, exercising Dou Rong's old Hexi prerogatives to appoint officers.

sentences.zh: 兄輔為驃騎將軍，弟驤為驍騎將軍，長子始為武威將軍，次子蕩為鎮軍將軍，少子雄為前將軍，李含為西夷校尉，含子國離、任回、李恭、上官晶、李攀、費佗等為將帥，任臧、上官惇、楊褒、楊珪、王達、麹歆等為爪牙，李遠、李博、夕斌、嚴檉、上官琦、李濤、王懷等為僚屬，閻式為謀主，何世、趙肅為腹心。

translations.literal: Elder brother Fu was nimble-cavalry general; younger brother Xiang was fierce-cavalry general; eldest son Shi was awe-inspiring martial general; second son Dang was garrison general; youngest son Xiong was forward general; Li Han was Western Yi colonel—Han sons Guoli, Ren Hui, Li Gong, Shangguan Jing, Li Pan, Fei Tuo etc. were commanders; Ren Zang, Shangguan Dun, Yang Bao, Yang Gui, Wang Da, Qu Xin etc. were claws-and-fangs; Li Yuan, Li Bo, Xi Bin, Yan Cheng, Shangguan Qi, Li Tao, Wang Huai etc. were staff; Yan Shi was plot master; He Shi, Zhao Su were belly-hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu became general of agile cavalry, Li Xiang general of swift cavalry, eldest son Li Shi general of martial awe, Li Dang general who garrisons the army, youngest Li Xiong vanguard general; Li Han served as colonel of the Western Yi while Guoli, Ren Hui, Li Gong, Shangguan Jing, Li Pan, and Fei Tuo led divisions; Ren Zang, Shangguan Dun, Yang Bao, Yang Gui, Wang Da, and Qu Xin formed his striking force; Li Yuan, Li Bo, Xi Bin, Yan Cheng, Shangguan Qi, Li Tao, and Wang Huai staffed headquarters; Yan Shi directed strategy with He Shi and Zhao Su as his closest confidants.

sentences.zh: 時羅尚貪殘，為百姓患，而特與蜀人約法三章，施捨振貸，禮賢拔滯，軍政肅然。

translations.literal: At time Luo Shang greedy cruel—became hundred surnames' scourge—yet Te with Shu people agreed three-chapter law—bestowed gave relief lent—ritual worthy drew stuck—army government solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang's greed tormented the people while Li Te issued a three-article code with the Shu gentry, opened granaries, honoured talent, and ran an army with crisp discipline.

sentences.zh: 百姓為之謠曰：「李特尚可，羅尚殺我。

translations.literal: Hundred surnames for them made ditty saying: Li Te still tolerable—Luo Shang kills us.
translations.idiomatic: Folk rhymes ran: "Li Te we can abide—Luo Shang slaughters us."

sentences.zh: 」尚頻為特所敗，乃阻長圍，緣水作營，自都安至犍為七百里，與特相距。

translations.literal: Shang repeatedly by Te was defeated—then blocked long encirclement—along water made camps—from Du'an to Qianwei seven hundred li—with Te opposed.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly beaten by Li Te, Luo Shang stretched palisades seven hundred li along the river from Du'an to Qianwei to fence Li Te out.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒遣督護衙博、廣漢太守張征討特，南夷校尉李毅又遣兵五千助尚，尚遣督護張龜軍繁城，三道攻特。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Yong sent protector Ya Bo, Guanghan prefect Zhang Zheng punish Te—Southern Yi colonel Li Yi again sent troops five thousand aid Shang—Shang sent protector Zhang Gui army Fancheng—three roads attacked Te.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Yong of Hejian ordered protector Ya Bo and Guanghan prefect Zhang Zheng against Li Te; southern Yi colonel Li Yi sent five thousand men to Luo Shang, who stationed protector Zhang Gui at Fancheng and struck Li Te on three fronts.

sentences.zh: 特命蕩、雄襲博。

translations.literal: Te ordered Dang, Xiong raid Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te told Li Dang and Li Xiong to fall on Ya Bo.

sentences.zh: 特躬擊張龜，龜眾大敗。

translations.literal: Te personally struck Zhang Gui—Gui multitude greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te led the assault on Zhang Gui himself and shattered his ranks.

sentences.zh: 蕩又與博接戰連日，博亦敗績，死者太半。

translations.literal: Dang again with Bo joined battle successive days—Bo also routed—dead great half.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dang traded blows with Ya Bo for days until Ya Bo collapsed, losing more than half his men.

sentences.zh: 蕩追博至漢德，博走葭萌。

translations.literal: Dang pursued Bo to Hande—Bo fled Jiāméng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dang chased Ya Bo to Handé; Ya Bo dashed toward Jiāméng.

sentences.zh: 蕩進寇巴西，巴西郡丞毛植、五官襄珍以郡降蕩。

translations.literal: Dang advanced invade Baxi—Baxi assistant prefect Mao Zhi, five-officer Xiang Zhen with commandery surrendered Dang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dang invaded Baxi, where assistant prefect Mao Zhi and clerk Xiang Zhen surrendered the commandery.

sentences.zh: 蕩撫恤初附，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Dang soothed newly attached—hundred surnames settled them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dang comforted the newly submitted townsfolk and restored calm.

sentences.zh: 蕩進攻葭萌，博又遠遁，其眾盡降於蕩。

translations.literal: Dang advanced attacked Jiāméng—Bo again far fled—their multitude all surrendered to Dang.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing Jiāméng, Li Dang drove Ya Bo farther off until every survivor capitulated.

sentences.zh: 太安元年，特自稱益州牧、都督梁、益二州諸軍事、大將軍、大都督，改年建初，赦其境內。

translations.literal: Taian year one—Te self titled Yi shepherd; supervise Liang-Yi two provinces military affairs; grand general; grand chief commander—changed era establish beginning—pardoned within borders.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taian Li Te styled himself governor of Yi Province, commander over Liang and Yi, grand general and commander-in-chief, adopted the reign title Jianchu, and proclaimed an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 於是進攻張征。

translations.literal: Thereupon advanced attacked Zhang Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against Zhang Zheng.

sentences.zh: 征依高據險，與特相持連日。

translations.literal: Zheng relied high occupied peril—with Te stood off successive days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zheng held the heights and skirmished with Li Te for days.

sentences.zh: 時特與蕩分為二營，徵候特營空虛，遣步兵循山攻之，特逆戰不利，山險窘逼，眾不知所為。

translations.literal: At time Te with Dang divided two camps—Zheng watched Te camp empty—sent infantry follow mountain attack—Te opposed battle not favorable—mountain peril narrow pressed—multitude knew not what do.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te and Li Dang camped separately; Zhang Zheng watched Li Te's lines thin and sent infantry along the ridges. Li Te counterattacked poorly; sheer slopes penned him in and his troops froze.

sentences.zh: 羅准、任道皆勸引退，特量蕩必來，故不許。

translations.literal: Luo Zhun, Ren Dao all urged lead retreat—Te measured Dang sure come—therefore not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zhun and Ren Dao urged withdrawal, but Li Te reckoned Li Dang would arrive and refused.

sentences.zh: 征眾至稍多，山道至狹，唯可一二人行，蕩軍不得前，謂其司馬王辛曰：「父在深寇之中，是我死日也。

translations.literal: Zheng multitude arrived gradually many—mountain road extreme narrow—only may one-two persons travel—Dang army could not advance—said his aide Wang Xin: Father in deep bandits within—is my death day.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhang Zheng's numbers grew the trail narrowed until men could pass only one by one; Li Dang's column stalled. He told aide Wang Xin: "My father is trapped among foes—today I die."

sentences.zh: 」乃衣重鎧，持長矛，大呼直前，推鋒必死，殺十餘人。

translations.literal: Then clothed heavy armour—held long spear—great shouted straight forward—pushed point certain death—killed ten-odd men.
translations.idiomatic: He donned layered armor, levelled a long spear, roared, and charged the van, killing more than ten men wherever he struck.

sentences.zh: 征眾來相救，蕩軍皆殊死戰，征軍遂潰。

translations.literal: Zheng multitude came mutual rescue—Dang army all fought-to-death battle—Zheng army then routed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zheng's reinforcements rushed up Li Dang's men fought to the death until Zhang Zheng's lines broke.

sentences.zh: 特議欲釋征還涪，蕩與王辛進曰：「征軍連戰，士卒傷殘，智勇俱竭，宜因其弊遂擒之。

translations.literal: Te deliberated wished release Zheng return Fu—Dang with Wang Xin advanced saying: Zheng army successive battles—soldiers wounded maimed—wits courage both exhausted—fit exploit their exhaustion then seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te considered letting Zhang Zheng withdraw toward Fu, but Li Dang and Wang Xin urged: "His troops are battered—wit and courage spent—strike now while they falter."

sentences.zh: 若舍而寬之，征養病收亡，餘眾更合，圖之未易也。

translations.literal: If release and widen him—Zheng heals wounds gathers fugitives—remainder multitude again joins—plot him not easy.
translations.idiomatic: Spare him and he will nurse wounds, rally stragglers, and reunite—far harder to destroy later."

sentences.zh: 」特從之，復進攻征，征潰圍走。

translations.literal: Te followed it—again advanced attacked Zheng—Zheng routed broke siege fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te agreed, attacked again, and Zhang Zheng fled the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 蕩水陸追之，遂害征，生擒征子存，以征喪還之。

translations.literal: Dang water land pursued him—then harmed Zheng—alive seized Zheng son Cun—with Zheng corpse returned him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dang pursued by river and road, slew Zhang Zheng, captured his son Zhang Cun alive, and returned the father's body.

sentences.zh: 以騫碩為德陽太守，碩略地至巴郡之墊江。

translations.literal: Took Qian Shuo as Deyang grand administrator—Shuo seized lands reaching Ba commandery's Dianjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te named Qian Shuo prefect of Deyang; Qian pushed downstream as far as Dianjiang in Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 特之攻張征也，使李驤與李攀、任回、李恭屯軍毗橋，以備羅尚。

translations.literal: When Te attacked Zhang Zheng—sent Li Xiang with Li Pan, Ren Hui, Li Gong garrison army Pi Bridge—to prepare Luo Shang.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Zhang Zheng Li Te stationed Li Xiang with Li Pan, Ren Hui, and Li Gong at Pi Bridge to watch Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 尚遣軍挑戰，驤等破之。

translations.literal: Shang sent army challenge battle—Xiang etc. routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang sent sorties; Li Xiang turned them back.

sentences.zh: 尚又遣數千人出戰，驤又陷破之，大獲器甲，攻燒其門。

translations.literal: Shang again sent several thousand go out battle—Xiang again crushed them—greatly captured weapons armour—attacked burned their gates.
translations.idiomatic: When several thousand more sallied forth Li Xiang shattered them, seized arms and armor in heaps, and burned the gates.

sentences.zh: 流進次成都之北。

translations.literal: Liu advanced halted Chengdu's north.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu advanced and camped north of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 尚遣將張興偽降於驤，以觀虛實。

translations.literal: Shang sent general Zhang Xing feigned surrender to Xiang—to observe empty solid.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang ordered Zhang Xing to sham defection to Li Xiang and scout the camp.

sentences.zh: 時驤軍不過二千人，興夜歸白尚，尚遣精勇萬人銜枚隨興夜襲驤營。

translations.literal: At time Xiang army not exceed two thousand men—Xing night returned reported Shang—Shang sent elite brave ten thousand mouth-plugs followed Xing night raid Xiang camp.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang had fewer than two thousand men. Zhang Xing slipped back by night to brief Luo Shang, who sent ten thousand picked troops muffled to follow Zhang Xing in a night strike.

sentences.zh: 李攀逆戰死，驤及將士奔於流柵，與流並力回攻尚軍。

translations.literal: Li Pan opposed battle died—Xiang and commanders soldiers fled to Liu palisades—with Liu combined strength turned attacked Shang army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Pan fell in the counterattack; Li Xiang bolted to Li Liu's stockade and together they swung on Luo Shang's force.

sentences.zh: 尚軍亂，敗還者十一二。

translations.literal: Shang army chaotic—defeated returned ones one-two tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang's army dissolved; barely one man in ten escaped.

sentences.zh: 晉梁州刺史許雄遣軍攻特，特陷破之，進擊，破尚水上軍，遂寇成都。

translations.literal: Jin Liang provincial inspector Xu Xiong sent army attack Te—Te routed them—advanced struck—broke Shang water army—then invaded Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's Liang inspector Xu Xiong attacked Li Te and was smashed in turn; Li Te smashed Luo Shang's river flotilla and pressed Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 蜀郡太守徐儉以小城降，特以李瑾為蜀郡太守以撫之。

translations.literal: Shu commandery prefect Xu Jian with small city surrendered—Te took Li Jin as Shu grand administrator to soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: Shu prefect Xu Jian yielded the lesser citadel; Li Te installed Li Jin to pacify the district.

sentences.zh: 羅尚據大城自守。

translations.literal: Luo Shang occupied great city self guarded.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang barricaded himself in the main enclosure.

sentences.zh: 流進屯江西，尚懼，遣使求和。

translations.literal: Liu advanced garrison river west—Shang feared—sent envoy beg peace.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu camped west of the river until Luo Shang, terrified, sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 是時蜀人危懼，並結村堡，請命於特，特遣人安撫之。

translations.literal: At this time Shu people peril afraid—together tied village forts—begged orders from Te—Te sent men soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: Shu residents, rattled, walled their hamlets and pledged loyalty to Li Te, who sent officers to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 益州從事任明說尚曰：「特既凶逆，侵暴百姓，又分人散眾，在諸村堡，驕怠無備，是天亡之也。

translations.literal: Yi clerk Ren Ming urged Shang saying: Te since fierce rebellious—invaded tyrannized hundred surnames—again divided people scattered hosts—among various village forts—arrogant slack without preparation—is heaven destroying them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Province clerk Ren Ming told Luo Shang: "Li Te is brutal and has scattered his followers among the stockades; grown arrogant and lax, they invite heaven's curse.

sentences.zh: 可告諸村，密克期日，內外擊之，破之必矣。

translations.literal: May tell various villages—secretly fix date day—inside-outside strike them—break them certain.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly notify every hamlet, fix a common hour, and strike inside and out—you will crush him."

sentences.zh: 」尚從之。

translations.literal: Shang followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang agreed.

sentences.zh: 明先偽降特，特問城中虛實，明曰：「米穀已欲盡，但有貨帛耳。

translations.literal: Ming first feigned surrender Te—Te asked inside city empty solid—Ming said: Rice grain already about exhausted—only have goods silk.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Ming first feigned submission; Li Te asked after Chengdu's stores and Ren Ming answered: "Grain is nearly gone—only cloth and coin remain."

sentences.zh: 」因求省家，特許之。

translations.literal: Thereupon begged visit family—Te permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to visit kin and Li Te allowed it.

sentences.zh: 明潛說諸村，諸村悉聽命。

translations.literal: Ming secretly persuaded various villages—various villages all obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Ming secretly canvassed the hamlets and won every pledge.

sentences.zh: 還報尚，尚許如期出軍，諸村亦許一時赴會。

translations.literal: Returned reported Shang—Shang promised accord date issue troops—various villages also promised same moment attend rendezvous.
translations.idiomatic: He reported back to Luo Shang, who promised to march on the appointed day; every village swore to rise together.

sentences.zh: 二年，惠帝遣荊州刺史宋岱、建平太守孫阜救尚。

translations.literal: Year two—Huidi sent Jing provincial inspector Song Dai, Jianping prefect Sun Fu rescue Shang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Emperor Hui dispatched Jing inspector Song Dai and Jianping prefect Sun Fu to relieve Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 阜已次德陽，特遣蕩督李璜助任臧距阜。

translations.literal: Fu already halted Deyang—Te sent Dang supervise Li Huang assist Ren Zang resist Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu had reached Deyang; Li Te ordered Li Dang's deputy Li Huang to aid Ren Zang against him.

sentences.zh: 尚遣大眾奄襲特營，連戰二日，眾少不敵，特軍大敗，收合餘卒，引趣新繁。

translations.literal: Shang sent great host sudden raid Te camp—joined battle two days—multitude few not matched—Te army great defeat—gathered remainder troops—led hasten Xinfan.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang hurled his host in a surprise strike on Li Te's camp. Two days of fighting left Li Te outnumbered; his army collapsed and he gathered survivors toward Xinfan.

sentences.zh: 尚軍引還，特復追之，轉戰三十餘里，尚出大軍逆戰，特軍敗績，斬特及李輔、李遠，皆焚屍，傳首洛陽。

translations.literal: Shang army led back—Te again pursued them—rotated battle thirty-odd li—Shang issued great army oppose battle—Te army routed—beheaded Te and Li Fu, Li Yuan—all burned corpses—sent heads Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: As Luo Shang withdrew Li Te pursued through thirty li of skirmishing until Luo Shang threw his main force forward and broke him. Li Te, Li Fu, and Li Yuan died; their bodies burned and their heads went to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 在位二年。

translations.literal: On throne two years.
translations.idiomatic: He had held power two years.

sentences.zh: 其子雄僭稱王，追諡特景王，及僭號，追尊曰景皇帝，廟號始祖。

translations.literal: His son Xiong presumptuously titled king—posthumously titled Te King Jing—when presumptuous title—posthumously honoured called Emperor Jing—temple title First Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li Xiong later assumed the kingship and posthumously titled Li Te Prince Jing; when Xiong claimed the imperial throne he honoured Li Te as Emperor Jing with temple name First Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 李流，字玄通，特第四弟也。

translations.literal: Li Liu, courtesy Xuantong—Te's fourth younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu, courtesy name Xuantong, was Li Te's fourth younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少好學，便弓馬，東羌校尉何攀稱流有賁育之勇，舉為東羌督。

translations.literal: Youth loved learning—skilled bow horse—Eastern Qiang colonel He Pan praised Liu had Ben-Yu courage—recommended as Eastern Qiang supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved books yet mastered bow and horse; Eastern Qiang colonel He Pan likened his courage to Ben and Yu and nominated him Eastern Qiang commandant.

sentences.zh: 及避地益州，刺史趙廞器異之。

translations.literal: When fled land Yi Province—inspector Zhao Xin esteemed him unusual.
translations.idiomatic: After taking refuge in Yi Province Inspector Zhao Xin singled him out for favour.

sentences.zh: 廞之使庠合部眾也，流亦招鄉里子弟得數千人。

translations.literal: When Xin ordered Xiang assemble troop masses—Liu also recruited village youths obtained several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Xin ordered Li Xiang to marshal troops Li Liu likewise enlisted several thousand clansmen.

sentences.zh: 庠為廞所殺，流從特安慰流人，破常俊於綿竹，平趙廞于成都。

translations.literal: Xiang by Xin was killed—Liu followed Te console drifting people—broke Chang Jun at Mianzhu—pacified Zhao Xin at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao Xin executed Li Xiang, Li Liu followed Li Te to reassure the refugees, routed Chang Jun at Mianzhu, and helped crush Zhao Xin at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 朝廷論功，拜奮威將軍，封武陽侯。

translations.literal: Court weighed merit—appointed Stir Might general—enfeoffed Wuyang marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The court credited his service with the title general who rouses might and marquis of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 特之承制也，以流為鎮東將軍，居東營，號為東督護。

translations.literal: When Te inherited regulations—made Liu Pacify-East general—dwelt east camp—styled East Protector chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Te exercised imperial mandate he named Li Liu grand general who pacifies the east, stationed him in the eastern camp, and titled him chief protector of the east.

sentences.zh: 特常使流督銳眾，與羅尚相持。

translations.literal: Te constantly ordered Liu supervise keen multitude—with Luo Shang stood off.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te habitually gave Li Liu the crack troops to tie down Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 特之陷成都小城，使六郡流人分口入城，壯勇督領村堡。

translations.literal: When Te captured Chengdu lesser city—ordered six commanderies drifting people divide mouths enter city—stalwart brave supervised village forts.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Te took Chengdu's outer town he quartered refugees from the six commanderies inside while stalwart captains held the rural stockades.

sentences.zh: 流言於特曰：「殿下神武，已克小城，然山藪未集，糧仗不多，宜錄州郡大姓子弟以為質任，送付廣漢，縶之二營，收集猛銳，嚴為防衛。

translations.literal: Liu spoke to Te saying: Your Highness spirit martial—already conquered lesser city—yet hills marshes not gathered—grain weapons not many—fit register province commandery great surname sons as hostage duty—send deliver Guanghan—bind two camps—gather fierce keen—strictly make defense.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu urged Li Te: "My lord has seized the lesser walls, yet hill folk are not gathered and grain and arms remain thin—register the leading clans' sons as hostages, send them to Guanghan under guard in both camps, concentrate your veterans, and tighten every defense."

sentences.zh: 」又書與特司馬上官惇，深陳納降若待敵之義。

translations.literal: Again wrote to Te aide Shangguan Dun—deeply stated accepting surrender as treating enemy righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Li Te's major Shangguan Dun to insist that accepting surrender must never resemble indulging the foe.

sentences.zh: 特不納。

translations.literal: Te did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te brushed the counsel aside.

sentences.zh: 特既死，蜀人多叛，流人大懼。

translations.literal: Te already dead—Shu people many rebelled—drifting people greatly feared.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Te fell many Shu towns rose in revolt and the refugees trembled.

sentences.zh: 流與兄子蕩、雄收遺眾，還赤祖，流保東營，蕩、雄保北營。

translations.literal: Liu with elder-brother sons Dang, Xiong gathered remnant masses—returned Chizu—Liu guarded east camp—Dang, Xiong guarded north camp.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu with nephews Li Dang and Li Xiong rallied the survivors at Chizu—Li Liu held the eastern stockade while Li Dang and Li Xiong secured the north.

sentences.zh: 流自稱大將軍、大都督、益州牧。

translations.literal: Liu self titled grand general, grand chief commander, Yi shepherd.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu proclaimed himself grand general, commander-in-chief, and governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 時宋岱水軍三萬，次於墊江，前鋒孫阜破德陽，獲特所置守將騫碩，太守任臧等退屯涪陵縣。

translations.literal: At time Song Dai water army thirty thousand—halted at Dianjiang—vanguard Sun Fu broke Deyang—captured Te-installed guard general Qian Shuo—grand administrator Ren Zang etc. retreated garrison Fuling county.
translations.idiomatic: Song Dai's thirty thousand river troops anchored at Dianjiang; vanguard Sun Fu stormed Deyang, seized Li Te's garrison commander Qian Shuo, and drove prefect Ren Zang back to Fuling county.

sentences.zh: 羅尚遣督護常深軍毗橋，牙門左氾、黃訇、何沖三道攻北營。

translations.literal: Shang sent protector Chang Shen army Pi Bridge—gate Zuo Fan, Huang Hong, He Chong three roads attacked north camp.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang ordered protector Chang Shen against Pi Bridge while gate captains Zuo Fan, Huang Hong, and He Chong struck the northern camp on three axes.

sentences.zh: 流身率蕩、雄攻深柵，克之，深士眾星散。

translations.literal: Liu personally led Dang, Xiong attack Shen palisade—overcame it—Shen soldiers masses star scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu himself led Li Dang and Li Xiong against Chang Shen's palisade, shattered it, and scattered his troops like stars.

sentences.zh: 追至成都，尚閉門自守，蕩馳馬追擊，觸倚矛被傷死。

translations.literal: Pursued reached Chengdu—Shang closed gates self guarded—Dang galloping horse pursued struck—touched leaned spear received wound died.
translations.idiomatic: They chased Luo Shang to Chengdu where he barred the gates; Li Dang charged in pursuit but crashed against a spear angled across the lane and died.

sentences.zh: 流以特、蕩並死，而岱、阜又至，甚懼。

translations.literal: Liu because Te, Dang together died—yet Dai, Fu again arrived—greatly feared.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Te and Li Dang gone and Song Dai and Sun Fu closing in Li Liu despaired.

sentences.zh: 太守李含又勸流降，流將從之。

translations.literal: Grand administrator Li Han again urged Liu surrender—Liu about follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Li Han urged capitulation and Li Liu nearly agreed.

sentences.zh: 雄與李驤迭諫，不納，流遣子世及含子胡質於阜軍。

translations.literal: Xiong with Li Xiang repeatedly remonstrated—not accepted—Liu sent son Shi and Han son Hu hostages at Fu army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong and Li Xiang pleaded in vain; Li Liu dispatched his son Li Shi and Li Han's son Li Hu as hostages to Sun Fu.

sentences.zh: 胡兄含子離聞父欲降，自梓潼馳還，欲諫不及，退與雄謀襲阜軍，曰：「若功成事濟，約與君三年迭為主。

translations.literal: Hu elder-brother Han son Li heard father wished surrender—from Zitong galloped back—wished remonstrate not reach—withdrew with Xiong plotted raid Fu army—said: If merit accomplished affair aided—covenant with you three years alternate be lord.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han's son Li Li galloped from Zitong when he heard his father meant to yield—too late to dissuade him—so he fell back with Li Xiong to plot a night attack on Sun Fu, proposing: "If we prevail, we shall rotate supreme command between us every three years."

sentences.zh: 」雄曰：「今計可定，二翁不從，將若之何？

translations.literal: Xiong said: Now plan can settle—two elders not follow—about to do what?
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong asked: "We know what must be done—if our elders refuse, what then?"

sentences.zh: 」離曰：「今當制之，若不可制，便行大事。

translations.literal: Li said: Now ought restrain them—if not able restrain—then execute great affair.
translations.idiomatic: Li Li answered: "Seize control now; if they cannot be swayed, do what grim necessity demands."

sentences.zh: 翁雖是君叔，勢不得已，老父在君，夫復何言！

translations.literal: Old man although is your uncle—situation not obtain stop—old father at you—what again speak!
translations.idiomatic: Though Master Liu is your uncle, desperate times grant no gentleness—your father depends on you; what further excuse remains?"

sentences.zh: 」雄大喜，乃攻尚軍。

translations.literal: Xiong greatly rejoiced—then attacked Shang army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong concurred eagerly and struck Luo Shang's lines.

sentences.zh: 尚保大城。

translations.literal: Shang guarded great city.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang held fast inside the main rampart.

sentences.zh: 雄渡江害汶山太守陳圖，遂入郫城，流移營據之。

translations.literal: Xiong crossed river harmed Wenshan prefect Chen Tu—then entered Pi city—Liu moved camp occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong crossed the river, slew Wenshan prefect Chen Tu, and seized Pi; Li Liu shifted his headquarters there.

sentences.zh: 三蜀百姓並保險結塢，城邑皆空，流野無所略，士眾饑困。

translations.literal: Three Shu hundred surnames together guarded narrows tied stockades—walled towns all empty—Liu wilds nothing to plunder—soldiers masses hungry distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Across Ba and Shu the people walled every hilltop; towns stood empty, Li Liu found nothing left to forage in the open country, and his troops starved.

sentences.zh: 涪陵人范長生率千餘家依青城山，尚參軍涪陵徐轝求為汶山太守，欲要結長生等，與尚掎角討流。

translations.literal: Fuling man Fan Changsheng led thousand-odd households rely Qingcheng Mountain—Shang advisor Fuling Xu Yu sought become Wenshan prefect—wished invite tie Changsheng etc.—with Shang drag-horn punish Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Changsheng of Fuling led more than a thousand households onto Mount Qingcheng. Luo Shang's staffer Xu Yu of Fuling sought the Wenshan prefecture to woo Fan into an alliance that could pinch Li Liu with Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 尚不許，轝怨之，求使江西，遂降於流，說長生等使資給流軍糧。

translations.literal: Shang did not permit—Yu resented it—begged mission river west—then surrendered to Liu—persuaded Changsheng etc. make supply give Liu army grain.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang refused; Xu Yu nursed a grudge, asked duty west of the river, defected to Li Liu, and persuaded Fan Changsheng to furnish grain.

sentences.zh: 長生從之，故流軍復振。

translations.literal: Changsheng followed it—therefore Liu army again prospered.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Changsheng agreed, and Li Liu's army rallied.

sentences.zh: 流素重雄有長者之德，每云：「興吾家者，必此人也。

translations.literal: Liu by nature esteemed Xiong had elder-styled virtue—often said: Raise our house—must this man.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu always respected Li Xiong as a man of elder virtue and often said: "The man who will lift our house is Xiong."

sentences.zh: 」敕諸子尊奉之。

translations.literal: Ordered sons honour serve him.
translations.idiomatic: He charged his sons to honour Li Xiong.

sentences.zh: 流疾篤，謂諸將曰：「驍騎高明仁愛，識斷多奇，固足以濟大事，然前軍英武，殆天所相，可共受事於前軍，以為成都王。

translations.literal: Liu illness severe—told generals saying: Nimble-cavalry enlightened benevolent—judgment many strange—solid enough aid great affair—yet forward army heroic martial—almost heaven assists—may together receive affairs from forward army—make Chengdu king.
translations.idiomatic: As Li Liu lay dying he told his commanders: "General of nimble cavalry Li Xiong is humane and keen—his counsel is inspired—enough to finish our task; yet the vanguard's martial dash seems heaven-sent. Accept joint direction under the forward commander and raise Li Xiong as Prince of Chengdu."

sentences.zh: 」遂死，時年五十六。

translations.literal: Thereupon died—age fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died the same year at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 諸將共立雄為主。

translations.literal: Generals together raised Xiong as lord.
translations.idiomatic: The generals acclaimed Li Xiong as their leader.

sentences.zh: 雄僭號，追諡流秦文王。

translations.literal: Xiong presumptuous title—posthumously titled Liu Qin King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xiong assumed kingship he posthumously titled Li Liu King Wen of Qin.

sentences.zh: 李庠，字玄序，特第三弟也。

translations.literal: Li Xiang, courtesy Xuanxu—Te's third younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang, courtesy name Xuanxu, was Li Te's third younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少以烈氣聞。

translations.literal: Youth by fierce temper heard.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he was famed for fiery courage.

sentences.zh: 仕郡督郵、主簿，皆有當官之稱。

translations.literal: Served commandery postal inspector, chief clerk—all had holding-office praise.
translations.idiomatic: As commandery postal inspector and chief clerk he earned praise for competence.

sentences.zh: 元康四年，察孝廉，不就。

translations.literal: Yuankang four—investigated Filial Incorrupt—did not take post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuankang he was nominated Filial and Incorrupt but declined office.

sentences.zh: 後以善騎射，舉良將，亦不就。

translations.literal: Later because skilled riding-shooting—recommended fine general—also did not take.
translations.idiomatic: Later the province nominated him fine general on account of his horsemanship and archery; again he refused.

sentences.zh: 州以庠才兼文武，舉秀異，固以疾辭。

translations.literal: Province because Xiang talent combined civil-martial—recommended outstanding unusual—firmly with illness declined.
translations.idiomatic: The province marked him outstanding in civil and military arts and nominated him for exceptional talent; he pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 州郡不聽，以其名上聞，中護軍切征，不得已而應之，拜中軍騎督。

translations.literal: Province commandery did not listen—with his name reported up—central protector urgently summoned—had no choice responded—appointed central army horse supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Local authorities persisted, forwarded his name, and the central protector sternly summoned him until he yielded and received appointment as cavalry commandant of the central army.

sentences.zh: 弓馬便捷，膂力過人，時論方之文鴦。

translations.literal: Bow horse nimble—sinew strength surpassed men—contemporary discourse compared him Wen Yang.
translations.idiomatic: He handled bow and horse with ease and surpassed ordinary strength; contemporaries likened him to Wen Yang.

sentences.zh: 以洛陽方亂，稱疾去官。

translations.literal: Because Luoyang just chaotic—claimed illness left office.
translations.idiomatic: As Luoyang slid into chaos he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 性在任俠，好濟人之難，州黨爭附之。

translations.literal: Nature lay in knight-errantry—loved rescue people's hardships—province kin strove attach him.
translations.idiomatic: His temperament ran to chivalry; he loved relieving distress and men of the region flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 與六郡流人避難梁、益，道路有饑病者，庠常營護隱恤，振施窮乏，大收眾心。

translations.literal: With six commanderies drifting people fled hardship Liang, Yi—road had starving sick—Xiang constantly guarded sheltered pitied—relief gave destitute—greatly gathered hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Marching with refugees from the six commanderies into Liang and Yi he fed the starving and nursed the sick along the road, earning devotion everywhere.

sentences.zh: 至蜀，趙廞深器之，與論兵法，無不稱善，每謂所親曰：「李玄序蓋亦一時之關、張也。

translations.literal: Reached Shu—Zhao Xin deeply esteemed him—with discussed military methods—none not praised good—often told intimate saying: Li Xuanxu covers also one era's Guan-Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Shu Zhao Xin prized him; whenever they debated tactics Zhao Xin marvelled and told confidants: "Li Xuanxu is our age's Guan Yu or Zhang Fei."

sentences.zh: 」及將有異志，委以心膂之任，乃表庠為部曲督，使招合六郡壯勇，至萬餘人。

translations.literal: When about have different ambition—entrusted him heart-loin duty—then memorialized Xiang as troop supervisor—ordered recruit assemble six commanderies stalwart brave—reached ten thousand-odd men.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Xin resolved on rebellion he entrusted Li Xiang with core authority, memorialized him troop commander, and ordered him to rally more than ten thousand stalwarts from the six commanderies.

sentences.zh: 以討叛羌功，表庠為威寇將軍，假赤幢曲蓋，封陽泉亭侯，賜錢百萬，馬五十匹。

translations.literal: For punish rebel Qiang merit—memorialized Xiang as awe-bandit general—lent crimson canopy curved umbrella—enfeoffed Yangquan village marquis—granted cash million—horses fifty.
translations.idiomatic: For crushing rebel Qiang he secured Li Xiang the title general who awes bandits with crimson banner and curved canopy, enfeoffed him as village marquis of Yangquan, and granted one million cash and fifty horses.

sentences.zh: 被誅之日，六郡士庶莫不流涕，時年五十五。

translations.literal: Day executed—six commanderies gentry commoners none not shed tears—age fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: When he died under sentence every clan from the six commanderies wept; he was fifty-five.
